one_line_contribution: The claim is that a retrieved memory block imprints its action/tool histogram onto an agent's action prior largely independently of the current state, and that because retrieval changes the block at every step, removing that component requires a per-retrieval probe-estimated logit offset (MAC) rather than a scalar context downweight (CFG/CAD) or a single bank-wide base-rate offset; the deliverable is a double dissociation on ALFWorld plus a causally controlled measurement of the imprinting effect.
closest_prior_work: Zhao et al. 2021 (Calibrate Before Use) is the threat the proposal underestimates, and not for the reason it concedes. Its content-free probe is defined *per prompt*: the probe is run with the demonstration set that is actually in context. That the demonstration set happens to be fixed across a classification benchmark is a property of the benchmark, not of the method. Under retrieval, running the same probe per query is the method as originally specified, not an extension of it, so the 'adaptivity dissociation' (P4) is a comparison against a degenerate simplification the authors introduced themselves; no calibration paper ever proposed the global bank offset. Two further items bite. (a) Zheng et al., ICLR 2024, 'Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors' / PriDe already estimates a query-independent prior over an enumerable choice set and subtracts it at inference with an instance-level, cheaply amortised estimate - structurally the same object as MAC over an enumerable action set, and it already prices estimate-once-vs-estimate-per-instance. (b) Fei et al. 2023 Domain-Context Calibration is essentially the 'real-state-averaged estimator' of E2c, so the proposal's own fallback estimator is prior art. Separately, Sanchez et al. 2023 explicitly support negative/alternative contrast prompts, which makes MAC a member of the contrastive-logit-adjustment family (subtract lambda times log p(a | block, null query)) rather than a different instrument from CFG/CAD (subtract gamma times log p(a | no block, query)). Both are one scalar times one log-ratio vector; the 'factorisation vs scaling' dichotomy in the Short Hypothesis is a rhetorical contrast between two choices of anchor prompt, not between two classes of correction.
strongest_objection: The headline effect sizes are unanchored to any estimate of available headroom, and by the proposal's own arithmetic the accept-case branch is the unlikely one. The pilot that motivates the work reports memory fixing zero items and breaking six to seven, and reports that simply cutting k already neutralises that harm. On 1,000 ALFWorld games the total damage MAC can undo is bounded by the uncalibrated-vs-no-memory gap, which nothing in E0 is required to measure before the confirmatory run commits: E0's gate only asks that injection move success 'in either direction' beyond the noise floor. If that gap is, say, 2-3 points, then P3 (MAC beats best-tuned CFG by >=4 points episode success) and P4 (MAC beats the global offset by >=4 points) are arithmetically close to unreachable unless CFG at gamma* is actively worse than doing nothing, and conditions (ii)-(v) of E5 will all land inside the 3.0-point McNemar MDE. The pre-commitments then fire: P3 parity reduces the paper to 'the channels are not separable in practice', P4 parity reduces it to 'classic contextual calibration transfers unchanged to agents'. Those are the modal outcomes, not the tail. Compounding this, gamma* and lambda* are selected on a 200-game validation split whose own MDE is roughly 6-7 points - larger than every difference the screening must resolve - so 'best-tuned CFG' is a noise draw, and the headline MAC-vs-CFG contrast inherits a selection bias in MAC's favour that no amount of held-out discipline in E5 repairs. A second, independent objection an AC will raise: E2(a) validates the probe by showing its estimate tracks the *designed* block share (rho >= 0.7), i.e. the probe is approximately a monotone function of the literal action histogram, and ablation (e) prices exactly that free zero-forward-pass estimator - yet (e) is an ablation, not a confirmatory arm. If (e) ties, the entire probe apparatus and the P0 gate are decorative and MAC collapses to 'subtract lambda times the log frequency of each verb in the injected block', which is a two-line heuristic and a sibling of the action-balanced-retrieval baseline in logit space. A third: E1's substitution design changes *which* memory items are present in order to change the share of verb v, matched only on mean retrieval score and token count. Mean retrieval score is not relevance, and Risk 6 concedes the substitution pool exists only for some states, so the effect is measured on a state subset selected by pool availability and correlated with how stereotyped the state's action distribution already is - a confound the mixed-effects correctness fixed effect does not absorb.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Run the literature search before submitting anything rather than pre-committing to run it; it has now failed twice and a third silent round is not a tooling excuse an AC can accept. 2) Make E0 measure and report the uncalibrated-vs-no-memory headroom on the 200-game validation split, then re-derive P3/P4 thresholds from it and publish a stop rule: if the headroom is below roughly 2x the confirmatory MDE, the confirmatory grid cannot support the double dissociation and should be replaced by the step-level test as primary. The step-level outcome (30,000 paired steps, MDE 0.9) is already the higher-powered instrument and should be the pre-registered primary, with episode success secondary. 3) Select gamma and lambda on the step-level metric, or enlarge the validation split, so hyperparameter selection is not noise. 4) Write down MAC's decode rule explicitly and add negative-prompt CFG - contrast prompt = injected block with a nulled goal - as its own arm in E5. If that arm equals MAC, say so and reframe the contribution as 'which contrast prompt should agentic calibration use', which is a smaller but defensible and still useful claim. 5) Promote ablation (e), the literal-histogram zero-forward-pass calibrator, into the confirmatory grid; it is the true competitor. 6) Add an adaptivity-matched, decode-free baseline (below) so P4 tests adaptivity rather than MAC's machinery. 7) Report imprinting on the states *without* an equal-relevance substitution pool via a weaker design, or bound the selection effect, so E1 is not silently restricted to a convenient subset.
missing_baseline: A per-retrieval adaptive injection budget: gate or trim the block at each step on the JSD between its verb histogram and the bank marginal, a quantity E0 already computes for free with no forward pass and no decode-time correction. As written, P4 contrasts a per-retrieval method (MAC) with a fixed offset and calls the difference 'adaptivity', but the only adaptive arm in the grid is also the only arm with a probe and a logit correction, so adaptivity is perfectly confounded with mechanism. If adaptive-k matches MAC, the novelty-bearing prediction is answered against the proposal and the paper reduces to the pilot's own volume lever made per-step. Also absent: MAC stacked on the k=2 volume reduction (the pilot-validated neutraliser - showing MAC adds nothing on top of k=2 would be decisive), the negative-prompt CFG arm described above, and any pre-registered MAC-vs-no-memory net-gain test - none of P3-P5 requires calibrated memory to beat having no memory at all, which is the comparison a reader actually cares about.
preprint_collision: The check is a self-declared failure for the second consecutive round: zero queries returned, no verified closest work, no verified gap. The honesty is genuine and unusual, and the graceful-degradation scenarios (a)-(c) are well constructed, but honesty about an unsearched claim does not convert it into a neutral - novelty here is simply not established, and scenario (c) in the authors' own list ('a preprint already establishes per-retrieval calibration under RAG-style variable demonstrations') is the one I would bet on, because kNN/retrieval-based ICL with per-query demonstration sets has been standard since 2022 and calibrating it is the first thing anyone tries. I cannot verify 2025-2026 arXiv from here either, but the burden is the authors'. Beyond that, the check omits indexed work it should already know without any search: Zheng et al. ICLR 2024 (PriDe) on estimating and removing a query-independent prior over an enumerable choice set, the substantial selection- and frequency-bias literature on LLM function/tool calling, and the fact that Fei et al. 2023's domain-context calibration is the proposal's own E2c fallback estimator. A collision check that misses prior work reachable from the Related Work section's own citation graph is thin independently of the tooling outage.
